### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, every trace contained A21, A22 and A23 exactly once: A21 was always directly followed by A22, A22 always preceded A23, and the position gap from A21 to A23 was always 2 [OCC001, DIR002, REL011, REL016, LAG001].
- In the later window, A22 appears in only about 53 in 100 traces (down from 100 in 100), while four activities never observed earlier — A27, A28, A33 and A34 — each appear in about 47 in 100 traces, once per trace where they occur [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005].
- In the later window, A22 and each of the four new activities never occur in the same trace, whereas the four new activities always occur together, in both orders and with no fixed internal sequence [REL017, REL018, REL019, REL020, REL025, REL026, REL027, REL028, REL029, REL030].
- In the later window, A21's outgoing transitions split from 100% to A22 into about 53% to A22 plus roughly 10–15 in 100 to each of A27, A28, A33 and A34; each new activity in turn leads to the other three and to A23, and A23 now comes after the new activities in about 47 in 100 traces [DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, REL012, REL021].
- The position gap from A21 to A23 is now 2 in about 53 in 100 later traces and 5 in about 47 in 100, matching a four-activity detour in place of A22; A23's mean relative position also moved slightly later, from about 0.53 to about 0.55 of the trace [LAG001, POS001].
- Separately, A06's outgoing mix shifted from about A08 39%, A09 35%, A07 26% to about A07 47%, A08 31%, A09 22% [DIR001].

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that, in the later window, an alternative route through A27, A28, A33 and A34 was inserted between A21 and A23: in about 47 in 100 executions A22 is skipped and all four new activities run once each, in no fixed order, before continuing to A23, while the original A21 → A22 → A23 route is still taken in about 53 in 100. The support is direct — A21's outgoing transitions split exactly along this choice, A22 and the new block are mutually exclusive, and the A21-to-A23 distance changed from always 2 to 2 or 5 — and consistent across occurrence, routing, relation and lag indicators; the number of qualifying items (47) is also far above the roughly 0.5 expected by chance under this screening, so sampling noise alone cannot explain the ensemble [OCC001, OCC002, DIR002, REL011, REL017, REL021, LAG001]. Limitations: zero participation in the earlier window only shows the four activities were not observed then, so a pre-existing very rare route cannot be ruled out, and the evidence cannot show what determines which route is chosen.

Other differences: A06's choice of successor shifted toward A07 (from about 26% to about 47% of A06's outgoing transitions, with A08 and A09 declining); this upstream redistribution is not part of the main hypothesis and rests on about 90–95 traces per window [DIR001].
